title: Edited slides that are also reordered are not reported as moved

evidence.quote: Slides are matched by PowerPoint's persistent slide id, so a reordered slide reads as "moved"

const moved = old.index !== newIndex;
const type = shapeChanges.length > 0 ? 'modified' : moved ? 'moved' : 'unchanged';

reasoning: When a slide keeps the same persistent id but both moves position and has edited shape text, `moved` is true but the `shapeChanges.length > 0` branch forces the change type to `modified` and increments `slidesModified`, not `slidesMoved`. Consumers relying on `SlideChange.type` or `summary.slidesMoved` will miss the reorder even though the module-level contract says reordered slides read as moved.
recommendation: Represent movement independently from content modification, for example by adding a boolean movement flag or by incrementing `slidesMoved` whenever `old.index !== newIndex` while still preserving shape modifications. If the API intentionally has a single primary type, document that and expose movement in the summary separately.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test file `packages/core/test/diff.test.ts` exercises text diffs only and has no combined slide reorder plus shape edit case.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create a slides diff where slide id `2` moves from index 1 to index 0 and one of its shapes changes text; assert the diff exposes both the movement and the shape modification, including the moved summary count.
minimumFixScope: Update `packages/core/src/diff/slides.ts` slide type/summary accounting for moved-and-modified slides and add a focused slides diff regression test.
